channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia exchange strikes, as relations between Trump and Zelenskyy sour
item.description: Ukraine carried out a massive drone strikes on Russia, which launched deadly attacks on its smaller neighbor over the weekend.

item.title: Rep. Don Beyer, D-Va., on Trump waiving sanctions on Russia
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel asks Democratic Rep. Don Beyer of Virginia about President Trump's decision to waive new sanctions on Russia.

item.title: Investigators search for cause of deadly fire at Canadian military base
item.description: Four people are dead and dozens injured after a fire swept through a Canadian military training base in Alberta. Officials say strong winds caused the flames to spread rapidly.

item.title: Michigan's Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed campaigns in GOP stronghold
item.description: Michigan's Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is campaigning in the GOP stronghold of Michigan's Upper Peninsula, an area that hasn't voted for a Democrat in Congress in over a decade.

item.title: Anxiety about reinjury can derail a return to sports
item.description: Psychological factors are critical in bouncing back from a sports injury. Researchers find that many people cleared to play don't actually return to sports.

item.title: Solar power is changing agriculture in Pakistan, but some fear it could cause issues
item.description: Solar power is transforming agriculture in Pakistan. But in a country already facing water scarcity and extreme weather, some fear their widespread use could cause problems.

item.title: The list of school shootings just keeps growing. Do we still feel anything?
item.description: People in certain jobs develop a working relationship with death — like nurses, soldiers and police officers. Thanks to so many school shootings, so are teachers and students.
